items.definition: Living together as a couple without being married.
items.example: Cohabitation moved their date, because the shared life came before the legal form.

items.definition: The state of a group in which marriage is entered later than it used to be.
items.example: Deferred marriage is the name for a group-wide move to a later date.

items.definition: The total of the ages in a group divided by the number of people in it.
items.example: The mean age moved up, because a few people married much later than the rest.

items.definition: The age in the middle of a list: half the group is older and half is younger.
items.example: The median age stayed where the middle of the group was, even as the mean age rose.

items.definition: A planned event moved to a later date.
items.example: The postponement had a reason, and the reason was the contract.

items.definition: The state of being ready for a relationship, in time, money and emotional terms.
items.example: Readiness was not there yet, and she said so plainly.

items.definition: The money part of readiness: a steady income, some savings and a housing situation that holds.
items.example: Financial readiness is the money part of readiness; the rest is not a number.

items.definition: How far ahead the decision can see, which decides how urgent it feels.
items.example: Our decision horizons are different lengths, and that is the disagreement.

items.definition: The timing of the people around you, used as a reference point for your own.
items.example: Peer timing says everybody my age is married; peer timing is not a measurement of me.

items.definition: The pressure a family puts on the timing of its members.
items.example: Family pressure asks about grandchildren at the table, and the answer is a plan.

items.definition: The three-letter code that names a currency in the standard ISO 4217, used by banks, customs offices and computer systems.
items.example: Write USD on the invoice, not the word dollar, so the system reads it.

items.definition: The money the law accepts as the final payment of a debt, so that no one can refuse it as the wrong money.
items.example: The landlord must take legal tender for the rent, even when he prefers a transfer.

items.definition: The smaller part of a currency, such as the cent of a dollar, that people rarely see.
items.example: The price is 12.50 dollars, but the money is made of dollars and cents.

items.definition: The value printed on a note or a coin, such as 20 or 500.
items.example: The shop keeps one drawer for the smallest denomination and one for the notes.

items.definition: The price of one currency expressed in the money of another currency.
items.example: Ask which day the exchange rate belongs to, because the number is only true for that day.

items.definition: The currency of the pair that the rate counts from: one unit of it is the thing you exchange.
items.example: In EUR/USD the euro is the base currency and the dollar is the quote currency.

items.definition: The currency of the pair that the rate is expressed in, so the rate says how many units of it you get.
items.example: The rate is given in the quote currency, so a pair written EUR/USD reads in dollars.

items.definition: An arrangement in which several states use one currency and a single authority issues it for all of them.
items.example: The euro area is a currency union, so one central bank issues the notes for every member country.

items.definition: The use, by a country, of the currency of another country as its own money, with no domestic currency issued.
items.example: The country is dollarized: the shops take dollars and nobody issues local notes.

items.definition: The act of lowering the value that other people attach to a person's work or judgement.
items.example: The devaluation was quiet: every meeting began with a small doubt about her work.

items.definition: A country where most payments are still made in cash rather than by card or by transfer.
items.example: In a cash economy, a market stall may not have a machine at all.

items.definition: The market that trades a currency outside the official channel, at a rate the state does not set.
items.example: When the official rate stops working, the parallel market sets the real price of the dollar.

items.definition: The habit of adding a small sum on top of a bill for the person who served you.
items.example: In this restaurant the service charge is on the bill, so there is no tip to add.

items.definition: The money a person working abroad sends to the family at home.
items.example: He sends a remittance every month, and the rent is paid from it.

items.definition: The unit of time equal to one sixtieth of a minute.
The SI unit of force.
items.example: Newton’s second law, mechanical energy, Ohm’s law, and a travelling wave are written below.

items.definition: The capacity to do work or cause change.
The speed of a body together with its direction.
Matter of a definite kind and composition.
A written sign that stands for a quantity or an idea.
items.example: Read the symbol, then the English name.

items.definition: A short piece of text naming an item.
A level of quality or a rule of conduct.
A wrong result or a report of a fault.
An illustration, or a numerical value.
items.example: Use this when the title names one figure.

items.definition: A file sent together with the email. It should be named clearly and referred to in the body.
items.example: Please find the attachment, called Quotation-March-2026.pdf.

items.definition: The set of assumptions a person carries about how other people answer when they reach out.
items.example: My working model says that people get busy and come back, so I wait.

items.definition: The person or relationship a person can move away from and still feel steady in.
items.example: His sister was his secure base long before he had a partner of his own.

items.definition: The event that makes a person read a partner as less available than the person assumed.
items.example: One missed call was the trigger, and the rest of the evening went into reading the silence.

items.definition: Describing a person who takes the partner's availability for granted and stays steady when it wobbles.
items.example: She is secure with him, so she says she is upset instead of guessing.

items.definition: Describing a person who reads any drop in a partner's availability as a sign that the bond is at risk.
items.example: When he was busy, his anxious side read the quiet as a message about him.
